eld.notes: ESL endorsement codes 488 (K-8), 489 (6-12), 490 (PreK-12). Praxis 5362 required (Professional Assessments Policy 5.105). Two pathways: traditional EPP-approved program, or TDOE's no-cost Additional Endorsement Program for already-licensed teachers (asynchronous coursework + Praxis), authorized under Educator Licensure Policy 5.502 (revised Feb 2025). ESL programs minimum 18 hours, 6 hours of college-level world language, aligned to TESOL P-12 Standards (Policy 5.505 §English as a Second Language). Practicum coded null because Policy 5.505 does not enumerate clinical/practicum hours separately for ESL — set by EPPs. 2024 update: TDOE moved EL assessment from WIDA/ACCESS to ELPA21 effective July 1, 2024 (first ELPA21 Summative Feb 5, 2025) and adopted ELPA21 ELD Standards in place of WIDA 2020. EL share rose from 4.6% (2019 baseline) to ~9% (TDOE May 2024 SBE workshop, 93,433 students); the current TDOE English Learners landing page (retrieved 2026-05-08) reports the EL count 'exceeded 83,000 in 2024-25' but does not publish a precise percentage, so the 9% / 2024-05-30 figure remains the most recent SEA-published number that can be coded precisely. NCES Digest 2023 Table 204.20 (Fall 2021) reports a lower 57,799 / 5.8% under a different denominator and is included for context.

sei.notes: Rule 0520-01-19-.03(8) requires annual ESL training only for teachers who provide Direct or Indirect ESL Services, not all teachers.

history.title: EPAA 29(100) document analysis (Leider, Colombo & Nerlino, 2021)
history.description: Leider, Colombo & Nerlino published in Education Policy Analysis Archives 29(100) a comprehensive document analysis of every state and DC's bilingual, ELD/ESL, and SEI teacher-credentialing requirements, professional teaching standards mentions, and EL-percentage figures, based on primary SEA sources collected October–December 2019. The 2019 coding of Tennessee's EL-credentialing landscape is preserved as a temporally-anchored research baseline against which the catalog's later verifications are framed.

history.title: ELP assessment migrated WIDA → ELPA21
history.description: Per the May 30, 2024 SBE workshop 'English as a Second Language ELPA21 Transition' presentation, Tennessee transitioned from the WIDA ACCESS for ELLs to ELPA21 effective July 1, 2024, with the first ELPA21 Summative administration on February 5, 2025. The transition also introduced new Tennessee ELD Standards (10) aligned to the ELPA21 framework. The TDOE EL Assessments page now references ELPA21 as the operative annual ELP measure.
